newsitem.title: NORWAY: Turkey protests to Norway over Kurd meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turkey protests to Norway over Kurd meeting.

text.p: Turkey lodged a protest with Norway on Monday after the self-proclaimed Kurdish parliament-in-exile met in Oslo.
It was the latest in a series of protests by Turkey to various European countries where the Kurds have held their quarterly meetings since the parliament was founded last year.
Turkey regards the assembly as a front for the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrilla group fighting security forces in southeast Turkey.
Ingvard Havnen, spokesman for the Norwegian foreign ministry, said: "The Turkish embassy has expressed its disapproval that the Kurds are here. Turkey has protested.
"We have said Norway has freedom of speech and freedom of assembly. We neither can't nor won't stop the exiled parliament from meeting here," he said.
Norway did not recognise the Kurdish parliament as a representative for the Kurds, he added.
More than 21,000 people have died in Turkey in 12 years of conflict between security forces and rebels fighting for autonomy or independence.
